topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: Well, now, the Lord has surely granted me a bit of favor. It's been nigh on two decades since I saw Tom last, and there he was, in the market, just as sturdy as an oak. I hadn't expected he’d remember the days we spent chasing rabbits and building hay forts. He didn’t just nod at me; he called out my name, as clear as a bell. "William!" he shouted, and I could see the old mischievous glint in his eye. It’s a fine thing, to find a piece of your past still lingering in another's heart. I told him of my crops, and he spoke of his travels, and we both knew, right then, that some bonds aren’t so easily forgotten.
